_meta.title: GridWise -- Team-Authored Edge & Corner Case Pack (Unofficial, Self-Test Only)
_meta.purpose: Supplementary self-test cases to probe paraphrase robustness, boundary values, multi-directive interactions, and malformed-input handling BEFORE submission. These are NOT organizer/hidden judge cases -- do not assume ground truth here matches the real hidden set.
how_to_use: POST each case's input to your own /optimize-energy and compare directive_interpretation against expected_directive_interpretation where provided.
For cases with expected_directive_interpretation = null, only check that your service responds with a valid, schema-conformant, non-crashing result (see reviewer_note).
For malformed_request_cases, only check HTTP status code and safe-failure behavior (no 500, no secret/stack-trace leakage), per malformed_input_cases[].expected_behavior.

hourly_plan reference schedules are intentionally NOT included here (unlike the official Public Sample Cases) -- verify battery/energy validity yourself with a small local replay script against the rules in the Problem Statement Section 09.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: solar_reduction paraphrase: 'X% drop' wording

operator_notes: Rooftop solar will drop by 70% between 1 PM and 4 PM due to haze.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: A 70% drop leaves 30% usable.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: 'drop by X%' means factor = 1-X, NOT X. Common LLM confusion point.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: solar_reduction paraphrase: fraction-word wording

operator_notes: Panel washing this morning will leave only about a fifth of normal solar from 9 AM to 11 AM.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: 'a fifth' = 0.2 factor.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Tests fraction-word (not %) normalization.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: solar_reduction boundary: total blackout (factor=0)

operator_notes: Total solar shutdown for emergency panel replacement from 12 PM to 1 PM.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Full shutdown = factor 0.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: factor=0 is valid & must still be applies=true (not no_op). Single-hour window edge.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: solar_reduction boundary: no actual change (factor=1)

operator_notes: Inspectors will be on the roof from 3 PM to 4 PM but solar output will not be affected.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Explicitly no output change; still a stated directive, not no_op.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Trap: model may wrongly mark this no_op since 'not affected' sounds like nothing happens. But an explicit directive with factor=1 is still applies=true per spec (any supported type != no_op requires applies=true). Teams should double check this interpretation choice against Problem Statement wording; treat as an ambiguous/discussion case.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: no_charge_window paraphrase: implicit/indirect wording

operator_notes: The transformer feeding the charger trips offline between 2 AM and 5 AM for scheduled maintenance.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Charger offline implies no charging possible.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Indirect causal phrasing, no literal 'do not charge' words.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: no_discharge_window paraphrase + single hour

operator_notes: For a five-minute relay test at 6 PM sharp, discharging must be suspended for that hour.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Single-hour suspension of discharge.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Single-hour window; whole-hour rounding of a sub-hour event.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: minimum_battery_reserve: percentage-of-capacity wording

operator_notes: Keep the battery at least 75% full from 5 PM to 8 PM in case of an outage.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: 75% of 220 kWh capacity = 165 kWh.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Percent-of-capacity -> kWh conversion using THIS scenario's capacity (220).

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: minimum_battery_reserve boundary: reserve == capacity

operator_notes: From 8 PM to 9 PM the battery must be kept completely full as a precaution.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: 'Completely full' = full capacity, 220 kWh.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Reserve == capacity is a tight feasibility edge; optimizer must pre-charge exactly in time given max_charge_kwh_per_hour=50.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: minimum_battery_reserve boundary: reserve below base minimum (should not lower it)

operator_notes: Try to keep at least 10 kWh in the battery overnight from 11 PM to midnight.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Stated reserve of 10 kWh, below the base 40 kWh minimum.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Directive reserve (10) is LOWER than battery.minimum_energy_kwh (40) base rule. Optimizer must use max(base,directive)=40, not 10 -- tests rule in Problem Statement 5.3/9.2 that directive reserve only ever raises, never lowers, the effective floor.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: max_grid_window boundary: zero import allowed (near off-grid)

operator_notes: From 1 PM to 2 PM, the campus must draw absolutely no power from the grid due to a feeder isolation.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Zero grid import permitted; demand must be met by solar+battery.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: max_grid_kwh=0 forces solar+battery to cover 100% of that hour's demand -- strong feasibility/battery-rate stress.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: max_grid_window paraphrase: 'units' ambiguity

operator_notes: Grid intake is limited to 160 units per hour from 6 PM to 8 PM under the new feeder rule.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: 'Units' interpreted as kWh in this energy context.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Tests whether the LLM defaults sensibly when units aren't stated as kWh explicitly.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: no_op: distractor mentioning numbers/percentages (false positive bait)

operator_notes: Cafeteria prices will increase by about 20% starting next month.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Price change is unrelated to today's energy schedule.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Contains a percentage + time reference, designed to bait a false solar_reduction/etc extraction.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: no_op: distractor mentioning battery-sounding words in unrelated context

operator_notes: The security team's radio batteries will be replaced during the evening shift change.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Refers to radio batteries, not the campus energy storage system.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Word 'batteries' present but referring to something unrelated -- lexical false positive bait.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: no_op: distractor about future/non-today date

operator_notes: Starting next Monday, the north parking lot will switch to solar-powered lighting.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Describes a future change unrelated to today's 24-hour schedule.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Mentions 'solar' but is a future infrastructure note, not a today directive.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Two notes, same directive type, disjoint hours (must not overwrite each other)

operator_notes: Panel cleaning cuts solar to 40% from 9 AM to 10 AM.
A separate cloud system will cut solar to 60% from 3 PM to 4 PM.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Morning cleaning reduces solar to 40%.
Afternoon cloud cover reduces solar to 60%.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Two independent solar_reduction entries with different factors/hours -- guardrail/optimizer must apply BOTH, not just the last one seen.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Three notes: two hard directives (different types) + one distractor, overlapping hour

operator_notes: Do not charge the battery from 6 PM to 7 PM for a safety check.
Do not discharge the battery from 6 PM to 7 PM for the same safety check.
The alumni newsletter goes out this weekend.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Charging disabled during safety check.
Discharging disabled during the same hour.
Unrelated newsletter announcement.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: no_charge + no_discharge on the SAME hour forces battery_action=idle, battery_kwh=0 that hour -- not contradictory, just fully locks the battery. Also exactly 3 notes (max allowed).

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Reserve + grid cap directives with overlapping but non-identical hour ranges

operator_notes: Keep at least 60 kWh in reserve from 5 PM to 9 PM for emergencies.
Grid import is capped at 170 kWh from 7 PM to 10 PM due to feeder work.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: 60 kWh reserve required through the evening window.
Grid import capped during the feeder-work window.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Hour ranges overlap only partially (19,20) -- tests that each directive's OWN hour list is respected independently, not merged/unioned incorrectly.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Vague time-of-day phrase (no strict numeric ground truth -- crash-safety check only)

operator_notes: Solar will be weaker than usual sometime in the afternoon because of clouds.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: No specific hours/factor given -- there is no single correct numeric ground truth. Use this ONLY to confirm your service returns SOME valid, schema-conformant entry (either a reasonable best-effort solar_reduction or no_op) without crashing, 500ing, or inventing nonsense. Do not treat as a scored case.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Contradictory-sounding but not actually a hard conflict (idle-forcing), single note

operator_notes: The battery must neither charge nor discharge between 4 AM and 5 AM during a full system diagnostic.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Diagnostic requires charging disabled.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: One sentence implies BOTH no_charge and no_discharge, but the schema only allows ONE directive_type per note. Correct handling: emit either no_charge_window or no_discharge_window as primary interpretation per the single-directive-per-note schema, OR flag as a design question for your README. This is intentionally schema-stressing -- decide and document your team's chosen behavior.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Full 24-hour directive window

operator_notes: Keep at least 30 kWh in the battery at all times today as a baseline safety margin.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: All-day 30 kWh minimum reserve.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: hours = all 24 values [0..23]. Below base minimum_energy_kwh (40) for this scenario's battery, so it should have NO real effect (base rule already stronger) -- but the interpretation entry must still be returned correctly.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Degenerate optimizer case: zero solar all day + flat tariff (cost is schedule-invariant)

operator_notes: The cafeteria menu changes tomorrow.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Unrelated distractor.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: No solar, flat tariff every hour -> total_cost_bdt is IDENTICAL for every feasible battery schedule (150*10*24=36000 BDT via grid alone, since shifting battery energy can't reduce cost when tariff never varies). Use this to confirm your optimizer doesn't do something invalid chasing a non-existent discount, and that end-of-day battery neutrality still holds exactly.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Optimizer stress: initial_energy_kwh == minimum_energy_kwh (no discharge headroom at start) + tiny rate limits

operator_notes: Keep at least 90 kWh in the battery from 6 PM to 8 PM for backup power.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: 90 kWh reserve required in the backup window.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Battery starts exactly AT its floor (50=50), capacity only 100, and charge/discharge limited to 10 kWh/hour. Reaching a 90 kWh reserve by hour 18 from a 50 kWh start with a 10 kWh/hour charge cap requires charging on at least 4 distinct hours beforehand -- tests whether the optimizer plans far enough ahead and respects end-of-day neutrality back to 50 kWh afterward.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.edge_case_focus: Optimizer stress: battery starts completely full (initial_energy_kwh == capacity_kwh)

operator_notes: No unusual operating conditions today.

expected_directive_interpretation.explanation: Note explicitly states nothing unusual; no directive.

directive_interpretation_edge_cases.reviewer_note: Battery cannot charge at all in hour 0 (already at capacity) -- must discharge or idle first. Also must return to exactly 150 kWh (full) by end of hour 23, which is a tighter neutrality target than usual.
